The concave roof is supported by two parallel [colonnades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonnade "Colonnade") to the north and south, which divide each facade into [bays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_(architecture) "Bay (architecture)") measuring 40 feet (12 m) wide. In the original portion of the terminal, there are 16 columns in each colonnade.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Jones_1962-32)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ashton_1961-43) The northern colonnade's columns (facing the [land side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_side "Land side")) are 65 feet (20 m) high, while the southern colonnade's columns (facing the [air side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_side "Air side")) are 40 feet (12 m) high.[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-58) The columns are all made of [reinforced concrete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinforced_concrete "Reinforced concrete"),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._223-59)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF-1961-09-60) which is [bush hammered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_hammer "Bush hammer");[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF_p._82-21) the [rebar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebar "Rebar"), or reinforcing steel, in the columns was manufactured by [Bethlehem Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethlehem_Steel "Bethlehem Steel").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-61) Each of the taller columns has 20 short tons (18 long tons; 18 t) of reinforcing steel, while each of the shorter columns is reinforced by 16 short tons (14 long tons; 15 t) of steel.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._223-59) The columns slant outward at an angle of either 10[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1960-7) or 15 degrees,[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Forgey_p241-62) counteracting the forces of suspension cables that carry the roof.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1960-7)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ashton_1961-43) At the top of each column are edge beams, which hold the roof's cables in place.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AR_p._178-63)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ichniowski_1996-64) When the terminal was extended west and east in the 1990s, the new columns were built to the same dimensions as the original terminals' columns.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Forgey_p241-62)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ichniowski_1996-64)

The landside columns support a canopy that protrudes 43 feet (13 m) above the landside drop-off ramp.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1960-7)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Armstrong_1960-14) The [curtain walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtain_wall_(architecture) "Curtain wall (architecture)") between the columns are made of glass,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ashton_1961-43)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Stroud_p._558-8) slanting outward at the same angle as the columns.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Wells_1962-65) Each glass pane is placed on rubber [gaskets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gasket "Gasket") and fastened to the columns using rubber strips;[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Grant_1962-66) these gaskets tended to fall off after they were installed.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Freeman_p._66-67) The [Pittsburgh Plate Glass Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Plate_Glass "Pittsburgh Plate Glass") made 70,000 square feet (6,500 m 2) of glass for the terminal, which were cut into 1,137 shapes.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-68) The window panes are embedded within aluminum frames, which are curved and tilt outward at their tops.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF_p._77-69) The curtain walls in the annexes are similar in style to the original curtain walls, though they use modern gaskets that were less susceptible to falling.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Freeman_p._66-67)

The roof is composed of [precast concrete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precast_concrete "Precast concrete") panels,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF_p._82-21)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AR_p._178-63) suspended between cables that span the width of the building.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Giles_1960-42)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Public_Opinion_1961-70) Nitterhouse Concrete Products in Pennsylvania manufactured the slabs.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Public_Opinion_1961-70) There are 1,792 concrete slabs in the roof, which each weigh 800 pounds (360 kg) and measure 7.5 inches (190 mm) thick, including a 1.5-inch-thick (38 mm) styrofoam layer on the underside of each panel. The slabs, which measure 8+2⁄3 by 5+11⁄12 feet (2.6 by 1.8 m) across, create a deck spanning 89,800 square feet (8,340 m 2).[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Public_Opinion_1961-70) The cables, similar in design to the suspenders used on [suspension bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspension_bridge "Suspension bridge"), are 1 inch (25 mm) in diameter[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AR_p._178-63)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Public_Opinion_1961-70) and are spaced 10 feet (3.0 m) apart.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Armstrong_1960-14)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AR_p._178-63) Concrete stiffening ribs encase each of the cables,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF_p._77-69)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_pp._222%E2%80%93223-71) preventing the cables from bouncing around;[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AR_p._178-63) these ribs are 14 to 16 inches (360 to 410 mm) deep.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ichniowski_1996-64) Because the columns are slanted outward, the ribs are about 160 feet (49 m) or 170 feet (52 m) wide.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF_p._80-72)

To improve acoustics, the roof dips at the centerline of the terminal,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Armstrong_1960-14)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Jones_1962-32)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ashton_1961-43) reaching as low as 26 feet (7.9 m)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1960-7) or 28 feet (8.5 m).[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Friedlander_1962-57) The roof's centerline slopes down from both ends toward a drainpipe at the center of the building.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Sehlstedt_1962-73)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF_p._80-72) The drainpipe is about 30 inches (760 mm) wide[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Sehlstedt_1962-73) and can drain 12,500 US gallons (47 m 3) from the roof every minute.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF_p._80-72) Water from the drainpipe is funneled into a [catch basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catch_basin "Catch basin") nearby.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-74) The roofs over the 1990s extensions are similar in design to the original roof.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Forgey_p241-62)

Originally, the terminal spanned 500,000 square feet (46,000 m 2).[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-World_Airport_Week_1997-75)[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-76) During a 1996 expansion, the size of the Main Terminal was more than doubled,[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Reid_1996-41)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Potomac_News_1996-77) increasing to about 1.1 million square feet (100,000 m 2).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-flydulles.com_1962-9)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Potomac_News_1996-77) The interiors were initially designed in a palette of green, blue, brown, and gray hues, to match the landscape.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Gustaitis_1962-78) Originally, the Main Terminal's upper level was for departing passengers, while the lower level was for arriving passengers.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Mehaffy_p._4.8-46) The west and east wings have a combined 600,000 square feet (56,000 m 2) and contain an additional basement level that is not present under the original terminal.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ichniowski_1996-64)

#### Structural and mechanical features

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Structural and mechanical features")]

The cable roof allowed Saarinen to construct the upper story without columns.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Armstrong_1960-14)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Jones_1962-32) The lower story sits on a concrete floor slab, and the upper story's floor slab is made of reinforced concrete. On the lower story, columns are placed at regular intervals, supporting concrete beams above; these beams are aligned with the colonnades on the facade. The lower-story columns flare outward at their bases purely for decorative purposes.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AR_p._178-63) The original interiors are divided into [bays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_(architecture) "Bay (architecture)") measuring 40 by 150 feet (12 by 46 m), spanning the terminal's entire width and corresponding to the facade's bays. Each interior bay could be configured with its own ticket counter, baggage facility, concessions, and two loading bays for mobile lounges. Saarinen's original design allowed 40 feet (12 m) bays to be added on either end of the terminal as necessary.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-79)

Saarinen's master plan for Dulles Airport called for service buildings both east and west of the Main Terminal; these structures were designed with low roofs so they did not obstruct views from the Main Terminal. The original service building, to the east, included equipment for hot and chilled water production.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-80) When the terminal was completed, it was cooled by two large refrigeration units, which had a daily cooling capacity equivalent to 2 million pounds (900 t) of ice.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-81)

[![Image 6: Interior of an airport terminal, featuring expansive windows and waiting people](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/2022-03-24_13_43_30_UTC_minus_4_Ticketing_and_check-in_section_within_the_main_terminal_at_Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_in_the_Dulles_section_of_Sterling%2C_Loudoun_County%2C_Virginia.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2022-03-24_13_43_30_UTC_minus_4_Ticketing_and_check-in_section_within_the_main_terminal_at_Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_in_the_Dulles_section_of_Sterling,_Loudoun_County,_Virginia.jpg)

Interior of the upper level, with ticket counters at left and the curtain wall at right (2022)

When the terminal was built, there were ticket counters on the upper level, and conveyor belts that brought baggage to a loading area in the basement.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Bradley_1962-82) The ticket counters were originally grouped into three clusters.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Sehlstedt_1962-73) In addition, there were various stores, three seating areas with aluminum and vinyl benches, along with two large departure screens.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Bradley_1962-82) The original design included very few stores,[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-83) since it was not originally envisioned as a place to spend extended amounts of time.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-84) When the terminal opened, there were 24 mobile-lounge gates.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Kohlmeier_1962-28)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Friedlander_1962-57)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Riley_1963-85) Many of the mobile-lounge gates were subsequently closed with the implementation of stringent security procedures, and some of these gates were infilled with glass in the 1990s.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Freeman_p._67-36) When the terminal was expanded west and east in the 1990s, stores and ticket counters were built in both wings;[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Reingold_1994-38)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Reid_1996-41) the annexes have similar terrazzo floors and concrete surfaces to the original terminal.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Freeman_p._67-36) Until the 2000s, the upper story also had security-screening areas.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-USA_Today_j755-86)

The lower, or ground, story initially contained regional and commuter airline gates, along with offices[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Rife_1968-53) and baggage carousels.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Mehaffy_p._4.8-46)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Cowan_1990a-87) The lower level also includes a "Dulles Diamond" security screening facility for frequent travelers,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Yu_2009-88)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_Washington_Post_2009-89) as well as baggage carousels and a baggage-sorting facility in the west wing.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Reid_1996-41) Escalators connect the upper and lower levels, allowing arriving passengers to pick up their baggage.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Armstrong_1960-14)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Giles_1960-42) The south concourse had marble tables and upholstered seats.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Bradley_1962-82) There was also a reflecting pool in the south concourse, along with lounges on a balcony level overlooking the concourse.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Gustaitis_1962-78) Basements under both wings accommodate baggage handling facilities,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Freeman_p._67-36)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ichniowski_1996-64) and there are two basements beneath the original terminal.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-USA_Today_j755-86)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Weiss_2008-90) The original structure's first or upper basement contains security checkpoints spanning 121,700 square feet (11,310 m 2);[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Yu_2009-88)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-91) the 8,500-square-foot (790 m 2) Capital One Lounge is located between the western and eastern checkpoints.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Clabaugh_2023-92) The second or lower basement contains a 54,500-square-foot (5,060 m 2) station for the [AeroTrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AeroTrain_(Dulles_International_Airport) "AeroTrain (Dulles International Airport)") people-mover system.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Weiss_2008-90)

The taxi and bus–limousine drop-off areas lead directly to the terminal's upper level, and a ramp and escalators lead from the private automobile drop-off areas to the upper level.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Bradley_1962-82) A 1,000-foot-long (300 m) underpass with [moving walkways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moving_walkway "Moving walkway") links the Main Terminal to parking garages and the Dulles International Airport station.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Cline_2022-93) The underpass is accessed from the terminal via elevators[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Cline_2022-93) and a pair of escalators.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-94) Another 1,000-foot-long (300 m) tunnel leads south from the Main Terminal to midfield concourse B.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-flydulles.com_1962-9) Escalators and elevators also descend to the basements.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-95)

[![Image 7: Airport mobile lounges stand next to a modern airport building](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/Dulles_International_Airport_mobile_lounges_00769v_%281%29.jpg/250px-Dulles_International_Airport_mobile_lounges_00769v_%281%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dulles_International_Airport_mobile_lounges_00769v_(1).jpg)

The terminal with its original mobile lounges (c. 1962)

Initially, after passengers were processed at the Main Terminal, they were transported directly to planes via mobile lounges.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-PA6_p._304-96)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Schwartz_p._50-15) The original mobile lounges were manufactured by [Budd Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budd_Company "Budd Company") and [Chrysler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler "Chrysler").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1961-97)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Roth_2025-98) They were similar to [airside transfer buses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airport_bus#Airside_transfer "Airport bus"), except that the lounges were intended as movable extensions of the terminal itself,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Mehaffy_p._4.8-46)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AR_p._180-99) with floors at the same height as the departure level.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-PA6_p._304-96)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Schwartz_p._50-15) Each lounge had doorways and adjustable ramps at both ends,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF_p._82-21)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AR_p._180-99) along with seats similar to those in the Main Terminal.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Bradley_1962-82) Though the floor could be raised and lowered to accommodate different plane models' heights,[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-PA6_p._304-96)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AR_p._180-99) it could not rise above 13 feet (4.0 m).[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1969-100) Each mobile lounge could travel at a top speed of about 25 mph (40 km/h).[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Friedlander_1962-57)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Riley_1963-85) Departure times originally reflected when the lounges left the terminal,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Kohlmeier_1962-28)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Friedlander_1962-57) and larger planes were served by multiple lounges.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Friedlander_1962-57) The Plane Mate, a variant of the mobile lounge, was introduced in the early 1970s[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Vanderbilt_j360-101)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Roth_2025-98) to accommodate [wide-body aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide-body_aircraft "Wide-body aircraft").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Pillsbury_1978-102) In contrast to the lower capacity of the original lounges,[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-104) the Plane Mates could fit 150 passengers and could rise higher than the original lounges.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1969-100)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-105)

Saarinen considered the mobile lounges a solution to three problems—they shortened the walking distance to the plane, reduced [taxiing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxiing "Taxiing") distances, and allowed greater [apron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airport_apron "Airport apron") flexibility.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Sehlstedt_1962a-29)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._216-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Roman_p._116-22) When the terminal was developed in the 1960s, jet planes could not fit traditional terminals and could only be accessed via long [jetways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jetway "Jetway").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Vanderbilt_j360-101) The mobile lounges eliminated the need for jetways[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._216-20)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1962-106) and allowed Dulles Airport to be built with a single terminal, smaller in size than other airports' terminals.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-McLeod_1959-12) They were also intended to increase operational flexibility, because planes no longer had to unload passengers next to the terminal,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._216-20)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Stepp_1959-107) while also reducing airlines' taxiing fees and keeping aircraft emissions away from the terminal.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Bennett_1964-108) Passengers also did not have to walk more than a few hundred feet.[[h]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-110)

Retrospectively, observers noted that the lounges were inconvenient to use[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-111) and that passengers making [connecting flights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecting_flight "Connecting flight") had to wait for multiple lounges.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Gottdiener_2001-112) When the midfield concourses were built in the 1980s, the mobile lounges began traveling to these concourses instead.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Schwartz_p._50-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Field_1999-16) The [AeroTrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AeroTrain_(Dulles_International_Airport) "AeroTrain (Dulles International Airport)") people mover system opened in 2010, traveling to midfield concourses A, B, and C.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-113) As of 2025, Dulles Airport's operator [Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Washington_Airports_Authority "Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority") retains 19 of Saarinen's mobile lounges and 30 Plane Mates, which operate to Concourse D.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-McCaffrey_v490-103)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Roth_2025-98) There are also plans to extend the AeroTrain to Concourse E, a future midfield concourse;[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-114)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Montgomery_h123-115) the potential expansion of the AeroTrain would make the remaining mobile lounges obsolete.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Montgomery_h123-115)

The [U.S. Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_United_States_Congress "81st United States Congress") passed the Washington Inner Airports Act in 1950 to provide funding for a new airport in the [Washington metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_metropolitan_area "Washington metropolitan area").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Mehaffy_p._S4-1)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-116) This directly led to the creation of what became [Dulles International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport "Dulles International Airport") in [Chantilly, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chantilly,_Virginia "Chantilly, Virginia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Mehaffy_p._S4-1) President [Dwight Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Eisenhower "Dwight Eisenhower") selected the 8,000-acre (3,200 ha) Chantilly site in January 1958,[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-117) and the U.S. government acquired the land that August.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-118) The airport was officially named in 1959 after [John Foster Dulles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Foster_Dulles "John Foster Dulles"), the [United States Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State") under Eisenhower.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-119) The airport and its Main Terminal were originally controlled directly by the U.S. federal government[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-World_Airport_Week_1997-75) through the [Federal Aviation Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Aviation_Administration "Federal Aviation Administration") (FAA).[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-120)

[![Image 8: Interior view of Dulles International Airport, with passengers at check-in counters and self-service kiosks, under a unique, vaulted ceiling and large windows](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/2022-03-24_13_47_19_UTC_minus_4_Ticketing_and_check-in_section_within_the_main_terminal_at_Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_in_the_Dulles_section_of_Sterling%2C_Loudoun_County%2C_Virginia.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2022-03-24_13_47_19_UTC_minus_4_Ticketing_and_check-in_section_within_the_main_terminal_at_Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_in_the_Dulles_section_of_Sterling,_Loudoun_County,_Virginia.jpg)

Interior (2022)

The [Civil Aeronautics Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Aeronautics_Administration_(United_States) "Civil Aeronautics Administration (United States)") (CAA) selected [Eero Saarinen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eero_Saarinen "Eero Saarinen") of [Bloomfield Hills, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomfield_Hills,_Michigan "Bloomfield Hills, Michigan"), in May 1958 to design several of Dulles Airport's buildings, including its Main Terminal and control tower.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_Washington_Post_and_Times_Herald_1958a-121)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-122)[Ammann & Whitney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ammann_%26_Whitney "Ammann & Whitney"), who led the airport's overall design,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._216-20)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_Washington_Post_and_Times_Herald_1958a-121) had previously worked with Saarinen on [Ellinikon International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellinikon_International_Airport "Ellinikon International Airport")'s terminal.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._216-20) At the time, Saarinen was busy designing the [TWA Flight Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TWA_Flight_Center "TWA Flight Center") at [Idlewild Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idlewild_Airport "Idlewild Airport") in New York.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Roman_p._111-123) Saarinen and Ammann & Whitney worked in collaboration with the airport's mechanical engineering firm [Burns & McDonnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burns_%26_McDonnell "Burns & McDonnell") and the consultant Charles Landrum to collect data for the design of Dulles Airport's Main Terminal.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._216-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Roman_p._116-22) They studied airport operations, including the distances passengers had to walk to access planes, at airports across the U.S.;[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._216-20)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Roman_p._111-123) the team found that, on average, passengers had to walk 900 feet (270 m) from terminal to plane.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-124) The design team was particularly focused on reducing passengers' walking distances, reducing [taxiing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxiing "Taxiing") costs, and increasing flexibility of the apron.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Roman_p._116-22)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AR_p._179-125) Furthermore, they anticipated that Dulles Airport would need 60 [gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gate_(airport) "Gate (airport)") by 1975 to accommodate increasing demand.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AR_p._179-125)

Saarinen sketched his initial designs on [legal paper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_paper "Legal paper").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-126) One early design proposal, by Boyd Anderson of Ammann & Whitney, called for suspension cables between the ground and roof; after Saarinen expressed his satisfaction, the design team instead proposed a cable roof.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Forgey_p241-62) The CAA reviewed Saarinen's preliminary ideas for the terminal in October 1958.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_Washington_Post_and_Times_Herald_1958-127) A key component of the plan was mobile lounges that would travel from the terminal directly to planes, eliminating many of the inflexibilities of jetways and fixed gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._216-20)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_Washington_Post_and_Times_Herald_1958-127) The terminal itself was tentatively planned to have separate levels for departing and arriving passengers.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-McLeod_1959-12)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-128) Contracts for clearing and grading the site had been awarded by the end of 1958, but no contracts for the terminal had been awarded yet.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-129) The terminal design was still in progress by early 1959, at which point it was planned to span 300,000 square feet (28,000 m 2).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-McLeod_1959-12)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Stepp_1959-107) Although no details had been announced at the time, the [_Evening Star_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evening_Star_(Washington_D.C.) "Evening Star (Washington D.C.)") described the design as "something revolutionary".[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Stepp_1959-107)

Saarinen's friend [Charles Eames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Eames "Charles Eames") prepared a short film about the mobile lounges to convince airport officials of their efficacy.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Roman_p._116-22)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-130) The FAA (then known as the [Federal Aviation Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Aviation_Agency "Federal Aviation Agency")) announced details of Saarinen's design in January 1960.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1960-7)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1960-109) The plans called for a 600-by-150-foot (183 by 46 m) double-level structure, with concrete piers supporting a concave curved roof; the building could be doubled in size.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1960-7)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_Times_1960-24) To reduce confusion, departing and arriving passengers were segregated on different levels.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Giles_1960-42) Saarinen and his associates wanted the design to symbolize the [Jet Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jet_Age "Jet Age") while also complementing the classical [architecture of Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Architecture_of_Washington,_D.C. "Architecture of Washington, D.C.")[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ashton_1961-43)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-131) The [control tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Control_tower "Control tower") and mobile lounges were designed in conjunction with the terminal;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1960-7)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_Times_1960-24) the lounges in particular made it possible to reduce the building's size, since long passageways were no longer needed.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-McLeod_1959-12)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Sehlstedt_1962a-29) The final design, including mobile lounges, was selected after the FAA examined over 100 proposals.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1961-97)

The FAA awarded contracts for the terminal's heating and cooling systems in August 1959.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-132) That October, it ordered a prototype of a mobile lounge[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-133) and awarded a contract for the terminal's telephone service.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-134) The FAA also built [settling basins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Settling_basin "Settling basin") for temporary use until a permanent sewage system for the terminal could be built.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-135) The FAA began soliciting bids for the terminal building itself in January 1960[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-136) and reviewed the bids the next month.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-137) The Corbetta Construction Company of New York City submitted the lowest bid, for $4,432,000,[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-138)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-139) and was subsequently awarded the construction contract.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1960a-23) That April, workers began grading the terminal's site and laying [foundations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foundation_(engineering) "Foundation (engineering)").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-140) Models of the Main Terminal were displayed at [Washington National Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_National_Airport "Washington National Airport") in August 1960.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Kornberg_1960-141) By then, the U.S. federal government (which originally operated the airport) had [oversubscribed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overselling "Overselling") all of the ticket counter space and the gates.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1960a-142)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Kornberg_1960-141) The demand for ticket counter space was already one-third higher than what was available.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1960a-142)

[![Image 9: Dulles Airport with a large tower on the left side of the image](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Dulles_International_Airport_%281970%29.jpg/250px-Dulles_International_Airport_%281970%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dulles_International_Airport_(1970).jpg)

The original terminal seen from the northeast (1970)

The Main Terminal's structural work was half complete by October 1960. At that point, concrete for the lower level had been poured, and workers had erected steel framework on the north and south side of the building, in preparation for the construction of the columns.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1960b-56) By the end of the year, the airport was unlikely to be completed by its originally-projected opening date of July 1961,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1960a-23)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-143) so outgoing FAA administrator [Pete Quesada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Quesada "Pete Quesada") postponed the opening date by one year.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-144) By June 1961, the airport's original $85 million budget had more than doubled to $175 million, and FAA administrator [Najeeb Halaby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Najeeb_Halaby "Najeeb Halaby") said the new terminal would be overcrowded by 1967.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-145) Due to a lack of federal funding, the building's initial length was truncated from 1,200 to 600 feet (370 to 180 m).[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ichniowski_1996-64)

The terminal was still under construction when Saarinen suddenly died in September 1961,[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-146) at which point it was budgeted at $12 million.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ashton_1961-43) For the construction of each column, workers poured concrete around multiple tons of steel [rebar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebar "Rebar").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._223-59)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF-1961-09-60) The rebar in each column surrounded a metal cage, from which a worker oversaw the pour until it was nearly complete; the cage was then encased in concrete.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._223-59) Workers pre-stressed the roof's cables by loading sandbags onto them, thus allowing the cables to carry the roof panels without sagging significantly.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Forgey_p241-62) The cables were strung between each pair of columns, then bent into shape using concrete blocks and encased in concrete;[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._223-59) their installation required many complex computations.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF-1961-09-60) The concrete roof ribs were test-loaded after being poured.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF-1961-09-60)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_pp._222%E2%80%93223-71) No stationary [scaffolding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scaffolding "Scaffolding") was used for the terminal's construction, though the roof was built using a movable scaffold.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Merkel_p._223-59)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF_p._77-69)

Thirteen airlines had leased space at the airport by late 1961.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-New_York_Herald_Tribune_1961-147) That November, the FAA awarded a concession for the terminal's bars and restaurants.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-148) The FAA paid $4.6 million for the terminal's first 20 mobile lounges that month,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hailey_1961-97) but the airlines hesitated at paying the cost.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-New_York_Herald_Tribune_1961-147) The airlines were also reluctant to give the FAA specifications for space at the terminal until they knew how much their leases would cost. As such, that December, Halaby threatened to take over the design of each airline's spaces unless the airlines provided specifications within two weeks.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-149) By then, the control tower was 60% complete.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-150) The airlines agreed to lease the Main Terminal's 456-foot (139 m) ticket counter in January 1962, having petitioned for a longer counter.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-151) Disputes over fees continued until that June, when the FAA and the airlines agreed on a schedule of operating fees for the mobile lounges and the terminal's space.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-152)

The terminal's contractors began working double shifts in April 1962 after Halaby threatened to penalize contractors for not completing the terminal by October 1.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-153) During mid-1962, the FAA solicited bids for the construction of service spaces for the airlines.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-154) Builders had difficulties constructing the windows;[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Wells_1962-65)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Grant_1962-66) as late as June 1962, none of the glass had been installed.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-155) Workers eventually built a custom protractor to cut the glass.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Wells_1962-65)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Grant_1962-66) Because the windows were to slope outward, workers fitted gaskets around each window to prevent them from tipping over.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Grant_1962-66) The FAA announced in August 1962 that the terminal and the rest of the airport would be dedicated that November.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1962-106)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-156) By then, workers were finishing the interior, while airport staff were practicing with the mobile lounges.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Grant_1962-66) Numerous shops had been leased out,[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Grant_1962-66) and additional retailers leased space at the terminal that October.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-157) As late as a few days before the opening, many parts of the terminal were still incomplete.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Bradley_1962-82)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-158) The final cost was estimated at approximately $16 million.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AF_p._82-21)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Rife_1968-53)

### Opening and early use

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Opening and early use")]

[![Image 10: The interior of the Dulles International Airport with the original terminal designed by Eero Saarinen](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/Dulles_Airport_terminal_windows.jpg/250px-Dulles_Airport_terminal_windows.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dulles_Airport_terminal_windows.jpg)

The western end of the terminal, facing the landside facade (2025)

On November 17, 1962, former president Eisenhower and U.S. President [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") dedicated the airport with a ceremony at the terminal, attended by an estimated 60,000 people.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Boston_Globe_1962-3)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Munsey_1962-159) The first passengers began using the terminal two days later,[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-160) and the terminal recorded 25,000 tourists on its first full Sunday of operation.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-161) Some final work was still ongoing,[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Munsey_1962-159) with 15% of the work still incomplete at the time of opening.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Howard_k402-162) The terminal quickly became a symbol of the new airport,[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Baker_1962-163) and it received positive acclaim, in part because its mobile lounges made the planes entirely [accessible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accessibility "Accessibility").[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Haugland_m168-164) Travelers often threw coins into the terminal's reflecting pool;[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Howard_k402-162)[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Haugland_m168-164) the proceeds were donated to charity.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Newsweek_1965-165) The FAA leased out a [duty-free shop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duty-free_shop "Duty-free shop") at the terminal in early 1963,[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-166) and a restaurant opened there that November, at which point the terminal was basically complete.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Howard_k402-162)

Dulles was initially considered a [white elephant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_elephant "White elephant"), being far from Washington, D.C., with few flights;[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Pillsbury_1978-102)[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Davis_1966-167) this had a negative effect on the terminal concessionaires' business.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1964-168)_[Newsweek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsweek "Newsweek")_ said that staff sometimes outnumbered passengers,[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Newsweek_1965-165) and _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ wrote that "the terminal has entertained nearly twice as many viewers as travelers".[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Loftus_z664-169) Another source said that "once a visitor could roll a bowling ball from one end ... without hitting anyone".[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-170) Conversely, the terminal was popular as a tourist attraction,[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Newsweek_1965-165)_[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles\_International\_Airport\_Main\_Terminal#cite\_note-Loftus\_z664-169)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles\_International\_Airport\_Main\_Terminal#cite\_note-McDowell\_p888-171)_ and the mobile lounges had become more popular than expected;[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Loftus_z664-169)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-172) many visitors paid just to ride the lounges.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1973-173) The terminal and airport continued to experience lower-than-expected patronage in the mid-1960s.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Newsweek_1965-165)[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1964-168) Two of the terminal's concessionaires had gone out of business by 1966, while other concessionaires paid discounted rents.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Schorr_1966-174) At that point, there were somewhat less than a million annual passengers,[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Davis_1966-167) and only half the mobile lounges were needed.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Schorr_1966-174) In 1968, the lower level flooded, causing some damage to the terminal.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-175) Patronage steadily increased; by 1969, some concessionaires had recorded their first profits.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-176)

### 1970s and early 1980s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 1970s and early 1980s")]

By the early 1970s, the FAA anticipated that the terminal's usage would increase sixfold, from 2 to 12 million, within a decade.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-177)[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Donnelly_1972-178) To accommodate the increased traffic, the FAA ordered additional mobile lounges and stopped giving tourists rides on the existing lounges,[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1973-173) and U.S. President [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") allocated $7 million for a possible expansion of the Main Terminal.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ashworth_1970-179) Early plans called for the building to be lengthened east–west to 920 feet (280 m), increasing hourly capacity from 1,650 to either 2,300[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ashworth_1970-179) or 2,500 passengers.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-St._Louis_Post-Dispatch_1970-180) The architectural firm [Hellmuth, Obata & Kassabaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HOK_(firm) "HOK (firm)") (HOK) was hired in December 1970 to prepare preliminary designs for the expansion.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-St._Louis_Post-Dispatch_1970-180) When the [National Capital Planning Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capital_Planning_Commission "National Capital Planning Commission") (NCPC) approved the plans in 1972,[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hodge_1977-181) the project was estimated to cost $12 million.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Donnelly_1972-178) HOK and [Peat, Marwick & Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peat,_Marwick,_Mitchell "Peat, Marwick, Mitchell") were hired to develop an expansion plan for the terminal, but no progress occurred for several years,[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Huxtable_o904-182)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ashworth_1976-183) in part because of funding shortages and insufficient demand.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hodge_1977-181)

[![Image 11: Exterior shot of the terminal building at Washington Dulles International Airport featuring large glass panels and a curved, concrete roof](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Dulles_Terminal_-_3.jpg/250px-Dulles_Terminal_-_3.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dulles_Terminal_-_3.jpg)

The landside facade (2023)

The expansion plans were renewed in 1976, when the FAA directed Peat, Marwick & Mitchell to revise the airport's master plan.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ashworth_1976-183) At that point, the terminal expansion was planned to cost $15 million;[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ashworth_1976-183) it was to be part of a $150–190 million overhaul of the airport.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Morris_1977-184) The NCPC expressed concerns that the east–west annexes would overshadow the original design,[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Hodge_1977-181) and preservationists advocated for the terminal to be designated as a landmark, restricting changes to the structure.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Huxtable_o904-182) Ultimately, HOK designed two small annexes along the southern facade for additional mobile lounge gates.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-A-1988-05-26) These annexes measured 50 feet (15 m) wide,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-A-1988-05-26)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Morris_1978-185) about the same as the mobile lounges' lengths, and were built in a similar style to the original terminal.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-186) The FAA hired Frank Briscoe Co. in early 1978 to expand the terminal,[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-187) and work began that September.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Morris_1978-185) The same year, the control tower's radome was replaced.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Kelly_j193-54) The project freed up space in the original terminal for baggage handling,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-A-1988-05-26)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Morris_1978-185) and the FAA awarded a contract to expand the baggage-handling facilities in late 1979.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-188) HOK's expansion was completed in 1980.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Freeman_p._67-36)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AJ-1980-11-189) By then, customs facilities had been moved to an adjacent temporary structure with four mobile-lounge bays.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-AJ-1980-11-189)

The expansion came just as patronage at Dulles Airport dropped sharply, in part because of the inconvenience of accessing and using the airport.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-190)[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Battle_Creek_Enquirer_c578-191) To attract business, the FAA began allowing small planes to load or unload directly at the terminal itself.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Battle_Creek_Enquirer_c578-191) The FAA rejected plans to add more airline gates to the terminal, citing esthetic concerns and a lack of space.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-192) Instead, in 1983, the agency proposed a "midfield concourse" in the middle of the apron, from which passengers could load onto planes directly.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-193) The first midfield concourse was hastily built and could be accessed only by the mobile lounges.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-194)

### Master plan expansion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Master plan expansion")]

#### Mid- and late 1980s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Mid- and late 1980s")]

In the mid-1980s, as part of a master plan, a consultant recommended doubling the Main Terminal's size, constructing a people-mover to the midfield concourse, and expanding the terminal's airline gates.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-195) New vehicular ramps were proposed to alleviate traffic in front of the terminal.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Henderson_1987a-196) The plans also included new facilities for several airlines that used the Main Terminal,[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1985-197)[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_Business_Review_1986-198) along with a separate terminal for international arrivals.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Henderson_1987a-196)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Cowan_1990-199) The expansions came amid rapid growth in the airport's usage, which neared 4 million by 1984.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-200)[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_New_York_Times_1985-197) The master plan was approved by the NCPC in 1986,[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-201) at which point was expected to cost $420 million.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-202)[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Henderson_1987-203) In the meantime, a clinic, baggage claim areas, and stores in the terminal were added, while the international arrivals area was revamped.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_Business_Review_1986-198)

The [Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Washington_Airports_Authority "Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority") (MWAA) took over Dulles Airport's operation in 1987 and assumed responsibility for the expansion program.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Henderson_1987-203)[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-204)[David Childs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Childs "David Childs") and Marilyn Taylor of [Skidmore, Owings & Merrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skidmore,_Owings_%26_Merrill "Skidmore, Owings & Merrill") (SOM) were hired to design a master plan for the terminal, which was rapidly approaching its annual capacity of 13 million passengers.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-A-1988-05-26) Passengers in the terminal frequently had to wait hours to get their luggage, and the [departure boards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departure_board "Departure board") could not display all the flights.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_Daily_Progress_1989-205) Concessions and security equipment had been installed throughout the years, intruding on the original interior design.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-206) Security concerns had also required the mobile-lounge docks on the south facade to be closed; instead, passengers had to undergo X-ray screening, creating a [bottleneck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bottleneck_(production) "Bottleneck (production)").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Freeman_p._67-36)

The MWAA banned smoking inside the terminal in 1988.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-207) The same year, to alleviate congestion at the Main Terminal, the MWAA began constructing the international arrivals terminal,[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-208) which was designed by SOM to the west of the original terminal.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Freeman_p._63-31) The MWAA also developed a satellite facility with a baggage check and duty-free shop in [Downtown Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_(Washington,_D.C.) "Downtown (Washington, D.C.)"), which opened in 1989, further relieving crowding.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-209) At that point, the Main Terminal's expansion was scheduled to be completed by early 1994.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-The_Daily_Progress_1989-205) In the meantime, the MWAA added temporary gates to the terminal, which consisted of [semi-trailers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-trailer "Semi-trailer"); since these trailers were intended as temporary structures, they did not need to undergo a historic-preservation review.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Reingold_1994-38)

A baggage-claim area was added inside the terminal in 1990,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Cowan_1990a-87) and a federal inspection area at the Main Terminal was enlarged as well.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-210) The International Arrivals Terminal opened in 1991, replacing the international-arrivals facilities in the Main Terminal,[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-211) though the new terminal quickly became overcrowded.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-212) The MWAA was also constructing permanent midfield concourses,[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-213) replacing the temporary annexes on the main building's southern facade.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-A-1988-05-26) The Main Terminal's annexes were tentatively scheduled to be completed in 1993;[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Cowan_1990-199) the extensions would incorporate a similar curved roof to the original terminal, which would remain visible from the Dulles Access Road.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-214) Despite calls by [United Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Airlines "United Airlines") officials to halt or delay the proposed expansion,[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-215) the MWAA decided to proceed with the renovation, the cost of which had risen to $319 million.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-216) The control tower's radome was replaced again in 1993.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Kelly_j193-54)

By 1993, workers had upgraded the airport's utilities to support the terminal's expansion, which was scheduled to be completed in 1996[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Fehr_1993-217) or 1997.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Moore_1992-218) This was planned to be followed in 1998 by the original terminal's interior.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Fehr_1993-217) By that time, Dulles had over 11 million annual passengers,[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Fehr_1993-217)[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Moore_1992-218)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Arch_p._40-30) and airport officials were considering replacing the once-novel mobile lounges with a people mover.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-219) Work on the expansion began in October 1993,[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-220) though MWAA officials were already contemplating further upgrades before work started.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-221) To fund the renovation, the MWAA added a [passenger facility charge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passenger_facility_charge "Passenger facility charge") to every ticket,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Reingold_1994-38) and it issued [bonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bond_(finance) "Bond (finance)") to cover seven-tenths of the cost.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Potomac_News_1996-77)[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Danville_Register_and_Bee_1996-222) The Main Terminal was lengthened to 1,240 feet (380 m), slightly more than twice the original length,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Cullerton_1996-39)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Reid_1996-41) and the vehicular ramps were also expanded.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Cullerton_1996-39)[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-223) The columns and roofs of the original building were recreated in the annexes,[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Forgey_p241-62)[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-224) though the annexes' roof cables were prestressed using cranes rather than sandbags.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Ichniowski_1996-64) The framework for the eastern extension was finished by late 1995, with the western extension still underway.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-225)

[United Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Airlines "United Airlines") moved into the eastern annex on July 1, 1996,[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-226) and the annexes were dedicated on September 6 that year.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Reid_1996-41)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Potomac_News_1996-77) Afterward, the MWAA announced plans to renovate the original terminal's ceiling, which required [asbestos abatement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asbestos_abatement "Asbestos abatement").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Freeman_p._67-36)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Reid_1996-41) The MWAA was also relocating the concessions to provide more space for queuing,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Freeman_p._67-36) and it finished replacing the vehicular ramps outside the terminal in 1997.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-227) Additional midfield concourses opened in the late 1990s, relieving crowding at the Main Terminal, where queues had frequently doubled back on themselves.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-Field_1999-16) At the time, there were proposals for an underground walkway (and, later, a people mover) leading to the midfield concourses.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-228) Development of the walkway was delayed after U.S. Senator [John McCain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain "John McCain") withheld congressional funds for the project, stemming from a dispute regarding flights at Washington National Airport.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal#cite_note-229)

[![Image 12: The AeroTrain station in the Main Terminal's second basement](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/2015-09-29_23_37_05_AeroTrain_station_at_the_main_terminal_of_Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_in_Virginia.jpg/250px-2015-09-29_23_37_05_AeroTrain_station_at_the_main_terminal_of_Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_in_Virginia.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2015-09-29_23_37_05_AeroTrain_station_at_the_main_terminal_of_Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_in_Virginia.jpg)

The AeroTrain station in the second basement (2015)

By 2000, there were proposals to renovate the original terminal as part of a $3.4 billion renovation of Dulles
